newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Fresh Israeli-Arab clashes erupt in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Fresh Israeli-Arab clashes erupt in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli troops firing rubber bullets wounded at least three stone-throwing Palestinian demonstrators on Saturday in fresh clashes in the volatile West Bank town of Hebron, witnesses said.

They said the clashes began when about 100 Palestinians hurling stones and firebombs charged at Israeli troops on the confrontation line between Israeli and PLO-controlled sectors of Hebron, home to 100,000 Arabs and 400 Jewish settlers.
Witnesses said Israeli soldiers deployed across balconies, rooftops and alleyways in the city's heart to square off against youths armed with bottles and slingshots.
They said an ABC cameraman was wounded when he was struck in the head with a stone.
Violence has raged in the divided town every day for a week, wounding scores of Palestinians. At least 40 Arabs were wounded in particularly fierce unrest on Friday.

The clashes underscored tensions over a three-month impasse in Israeli-Palestine Liberation Organisation (PLO) peace moves sparked by Israel's ground-breaking on a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem.

The Palestinian Authority said in a statement issued after Friday night's cabinet meeting that Israeli settlement policies were the cause of the clashes and blasted Israel for opening fire on demonstrators.

"The Palestinian Authority condemned Israeli troops for firing live and rubber bullets and tear gas at our people...who are defending their land threatened by the crawling settlements," the statement said.
Israel has accused the PLO of orchestrating the unrest.

Clashes erupted in Hebron last Saturday after a U.S. congressional vote demanded President Bill Clinton recognise Arab East Jerusalem -- revered by Palestinians as the capital of their future state -- as part of Israel's capital.

Palestinian police have largely refrained from intervening in the clashes during most of the week. PLO officials have said that the Palestinian Authority was not ready to enter into a conflict with its people at a time when Israel insists on proceeding with settlement building.

Israel handed over 80 percent of Hebron to the PLO in January under a peace deal but kept troops behind to guard the heavily-fortified Jewish enclaves in the city revered by Moslems and Jews as the burial place of the biblical Abraham.
